key_learning_outcomes.label: C
items: Students analyze how character, setting, and plot interact, analyze two or more themes, analyze how authors individualize characters' perspectives, and analyze structure, sound, imagery, and figurative language in poetry.

Students analyze how informational sections and features convey purpose, analyze central ideas, explain rhetorical appeals and figurative language, and track how arguments are developed and how they could be improved.
Students analyze figurative language and symbolism, paraphrase grade-level texts, compare archetypes, and explain how rhetorical devices support an appeal.
Students write narratives, arguments that rebut a counterclaim, and expository texts from multiple sources, follow grade-level conventions, research with multiple sources, and present orally.
Students use academic vocabulary, Greek and Latin roots and affixes, and context to determine connotative and denotative meanings, and use digital tools and media.

version_and_update_notes.standards_version: Florida's State Academic Standards (B.E.S.T.) English Language Arts, 2025
notes: Organization: by_grade (ELA.8 codes). The book introduces a 6th-8th grade band, but these benchmarks are grade 8, not a named course.
Benchmark statements extracted from the rule-adopted 2025 PDF (Ref-18865), printed pages 95-99. Clarifications, sample texts, and convention skill lists are not stored in standard text.
No foundational-reading benchmarks (ELA.8.F) are printed for grade 8. ELA.8.C.1.1 is not in the grade 8 list; writing benchmarks start at ELA.8.C.1.2.
ELA.8.C.5.2 on printed page 98 has no terminal period. The K-12 progression chart elsewhere in the same PDF prints a period after "writing." The grade-page wording is stored.
